title: Base-flat polynomial modules: ordinary Tor bound and base derived tensor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n\geq0$ an integer, and $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $M$ be a $P$-module whose restriction along $R\to P$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Use first-variable ordinary module Tor [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] and ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor computed on K-flat first complexes as in [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model]. For every $R$-module $L$ there is an isomorphism in $D(R)$ $$M[0]\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L[0]\cong(M\otimes_RL)[0],$$ and $\operatorname{Tor}^R_j(M,L)=0$ for every $j>0$. For every $P$-module $N$ one has $\operatorname{Tor}^P_j(M,N)=0$ for every $j>n$. No finite-generation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed. The cases $n=0$, $M=0$ and the zero ring are included.

source.place: Tag 068X, lemma-perfect-over-polynomial-ring, base-to-polynomial Tor-bound input; ordinary-module quantitative refinement using the existing general polynomial Tor bound. Base derived tensor computation: section-derived-tensor-product.

proof.text: Regard $M$ as an $R$-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], its tensor functors preserve exact sequences. The complex $M[0]$ has flat terms (the zero terms have zero tensor functors) and is bounded above by zero. Apply [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]; the equivalent categorical convention in [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] makes $M[0]$ an admissible first complex for [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model]. Apply that comparison with second complex $L[0]$. In degree $q$, the total tensor has only the summand with both indices zero when $q=0$, and otherwise is zero; its differentials vanish. Thus it is $(M\otimes_R L)[0]$, giving the asserted isomorphism in $D(R)$ for every $L$, without any flatness condition on $L$.

source.place: Tags 064K (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism), 06XZ (definition-K-flat), 06XY (section-derived-tensor-product); ordinary-module first-factor model of the cited node.

proof.text: Compute ordinary Tor independently of the derived-category convention. For any $R$-module $L$, choose a projective resolution $F_\bullet\to L$ as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. For every $j>0$ the sequence $F_{j+1}\to F_j\to F_{j-1}$ is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], tensoring this sequence with the flat module $M$ remains exact, so $H_j(F_\bullet\otimes_R M)=0$. The definition identifies this homology with $\operatorname{Tor}^R_j(L,M)$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry], applied over the commutative ring $R$, identifies $\operatorname{Tor}^R_j(M,L)$ with $\operatorname{Tor}^R_j(L,M)$, and hence with zero. This supplies first-variable ordinary Tor vanishing for every test module $L$.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), exact tensor criterion; Tag 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right), symmetry of projective-resolution Tor.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-polynomial-tor-bound] with $A=R$, the given polynomial $P$-module $M$, the given natural number $n$, and $d=0$. Step 2 supplies precisely its hypothesis for the restriction along $R\to P$: all ordinary $\operatorname{Tor}^R_j(M,L)$ vanish when $j>0$. Its conclusion is $\operatorname{Tor}^P_j(M,N)=0$ when $j>0+n=n$, for every $P$-module $N$. The cited result has no finiteness hypotheses and explicitly permits $n=0$, $d=0$, and the zero ring and module. Step 1 likewise used no finiteness condition. When $M=0$ all displayed tensors are zero; over the zero ring every unital module is zero. Thus all specified boundary cases are retained.
